title: Scrap tyre recycling process with molten zinc as direct heat transfer and solids separation fluid: A new reactor concept
author: Riedewald, Goode, et al.
materials: The operating temperature of the molten zinc was measured using an Ashcroft temperature gauge (range of 0–500 °C, with a 1% ASME B40.3, Grade A accuracy) inserted into a thermowell manufactured from 316L stainless steel. The operating temperature was controlled by manually adjusting up to seven blow torches.

steps.title: Load tyre pieces and purge chamber
steps.instruction: Place tyre pieces side‑by‑side in leg A of the reactor, close leg A, then purge the chamber with nitrogen at 10 Nm³ h⁻¹ for 1 minute; afterwards reduce the nitrogen flow to approximately 1 Nm³ h⁻¹ to maintain an inert atmosphere throughout the experiment.

steps.title: Measure and control molten zinc temperature
steps.instruction: Insert an Ashcroft temperature gauge (range 0–500 °C, 1 % ASME B40.3 Grade A accuracy) into a 316L stainless‑steel thermowell; manually adjust up to seven blow torches until the molten zinc reaches and stabilises at 450–470 °C.

steps.title: Run pyrolysis until gas cessation
steps.instruction: Maintain the molten zinc at 450–470 °C while observing the glass flask positioned inside a fume hood; continue heating until no visible pyrolysis gases enter the flask, then turn off all burners.

steps.title: Cool reactor and stop nitrogen
steps.instruction: Allow the reactor to cool naturally to ambient temperature; once ambient temperature is reached, stop the nitrogen flow while keeping leg A sealed until cooling is complete.

steps.title: Open reactor and inspect
steps.instruction: Open leg A of the pyrolysis reactor for visual inspection of the solid residues.

steps.title: Recover steel wires from leg B
steps.instruction: Using two twisted steel wires each 300 mm long (one bent into a small hook), insert the wires into leg B and fish out the steel wires that have sunk to the bottom (Area C) while the molten zinc remains at 450–470 °C.

steps.title: Remove and weigh remaining tyre pieces
steps.instruction: Retrieve any intact tyre pieces that did not disintegrate, weigh each piece on a Sartorius ED4202S laboratory scale (maximum 4200 g, resolution 0.01 g), and record the weight loss (expected >50 % of the original mass).
